claims: C1 the role of a message specifies the source of that message
C2 the role of a message determines the authority of instructions in the case of conflicts, as described by the levels of authority and chain of command

concepts.name: message_role_definition
concepts.gloss: the role of a message (system, developer, user, assistant, tool) specifies the source of that message

concepts.name: message_role
concepts.gloss: message M has role R, where R is one of system, developer, user, assistant, or tool

concepts.name: message_source
concepts.gloss: message M originates from source S, as specified by its role

concepts.name: message_instruction
concepts.gloss: instruction I is conveyed by message M
concepts.inference: the clause speaks of instructions in messages, so a relation between an instruction and the message that carries it is needed

concepts.name: instruction_authority
concepts.gloss: instruction I has authority level L, determined by the role of the message conveying it
concepts.inference: the clause says roles determine the authority of instructions, so each instruction must carry an authority level derived from its message's role

concepts.name: conflicting_instructions
concepts.gloss: instruction I conflicts with instruction J
concepts.inference: the clause speaks of conflicts between instructions, so a relation identifying which instructions conflict is needed

concepts.name: authority_levels_hierarchy
concepts.gloss: the ranking of instruction authority levels: root > system > developer > user > guideline > no authority, used to determine which instruction prevails in conflicts

concepts.name: chain_of_command_principle
concepts.gloss: the principle that instructions with higher authority override those with lower authority, designed to maximize steerability and control

ontology.gloss: message M's role R specifies its source S
instruction I has authority level L because its message has role R, which maps to L in the authority hierarchy
ontology.body: message_instruction(I, M), message_role(M, R), authority_levels_hierarchy(R, L)
